Chapter 17: Lessons for Community and Leadership.
When you look at the stories of the apostles, it’s clear—they’re more than just tales from the past. They’re a sort of blueprint for building strong, healthy communities, even today.
Their journey wasn’t smooth. There was diversity, disagreement, and a whole lot of growth along the way. They had to learn to really listen to each other, to forgive, and to adapt when things changed.
And you know what? When conflict came up, they didn’t just sweep it under the rug. They faced it, head-on. They weren’t out to win arguments—they wanted to understand each other. Every person’s voice mattered, and they knew everyone brought something valuable to the table. For them, leadership was never about chasing status. It was all about serving others.
Of course, they made mistakes—sometimes big ones. But instead of getting stuck, they learned from those slip-ups and kept moving forward. Their humility, their honesty, and their willingness to change—that’s what held their community together.
Most of us, when we hit rough patches, wish there were quick fixes. But if you look at the apostles’ example, there’s a different path. One that calls for patience, persistence, and the kind of courage that keeps you going, even when things get tough.
So, if you’re hoping to build or lead a community, there’s real, practical wisdom here. Community can be messy—no way around it. But it’s in that mess where transformation happens. The work is hard, sure. But the rewards? They’re deep, and they last.
